The first public release of Job Search HQ: an AI job-search partner that works from your real experience. It's a folder you open in **Claude** (the Claude desktop app's Code tab, or Claude Code in the terminal) or **Codex** (the ChatGPT desktop app or the terminal). You talk to it in plain words; it finds jobs that fit you, writes resumes and cover letters from your own experience, tracks every application, runs mock interviews and drafts follow-ups. Nothing is sent or submitted unless you do it yourself. No coding needed.

## Which file to download

Under **Assets** below, download **`job-search-hq.zip`**. That's the app.

- `job-search-hq-1.0.0.zip` is the same file with the version number in its name.
- `job-search-hq-1.0.0.zip.sha256` lets you check the download (see the end of these notes). You don't need it.
- **Skip "Source code (zip)" and "Source code (tar.gz)".** GitHub adds those to every release. They're a copy of the whole repository, including the files used to build and test the app, and they're meant for developers.

## Get started

1. **Unzip it.** Mac: double-click it. Windows: right-click the zip → **Properties** → tick **Unblock** → **OK**, then right-click it → **Extract All** (without Unblock, Windows can block the folder's scripts).
2. **Find the right folder.** You'll get a folder called `job-search-hq-1.0.0`. Move it somewhere you'll keep it, like Documents, and check that `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are directly inside it. If Windows made a folder inside a folder, use the inner one. Put your resume in its `imports` folder.
3. **Open the folder in your AI app and trust it.**
   - Claude desktop app: **Code** tab → **Local** → **Open folder** → pick the folder → **Trust**.
   - ChatGPT desktop app: switch to **Codex** → add the folder as a local project → trust it → at **Hooks need review**, choose **Trust all and continue**.
   - Terminal: run `claude` or `codex` in the folder and trust it (in Codex, also approve its hooks with `/hooks`).
4. **Start setup.** In Claude, type `/start`. In Codex, type **set me up**. It's a conversation of about 14 short questions, roughly 20 minutes, and you can stop and pick up later.

Want to look around first? Ask for **the sample workspace**: a separate practice copy filled with a made-up job search, so you can try everything before you share anything.

Every step in more detail, with what you'll see: [Quick start](https://github.com/ClarvAI/job-search-hq/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#quick-start) and the [full setup guide](https://github.com/ClarvAI/job-search-hq/blob/v1.0.0/docs/getting-started.md).

## What you need

- **Claude** on a plan that includes Claude Code (desktop app 2.1.286 or later, terminal 2.1.287 or later), **or Codex** on a ChatGPT plan that includes it. Plans change often: see [Claude plans](https://claude.com/pricing) and [Codex plans](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing).
- **Windows with Claude:** install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) first. Claude needs it to run the folder's safety check.
- **Optional:** Chrome or Edge to make PDFs, [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) to change the look of your pages, and Gmail and Google Calendar if you want reply tracking and interview events.

## What it does

- **Finds jobs that fit you**, flags scams and stale postings, and saves each posting before it disappears.
- **Writes from your real experience.** Resumes and cover letters are built from your master resume, fact-checked against it, and saved as PDFs.
- **Tracks everything** in a spreadsheet you own (it opens in Excel), with follow-up dates and a networking list.
- **Drafts your messages** (follow-ups, thank-you notes, referral asks) into an Outbox for you to send.
- **Prepares you for interviews** with a company brief, your best stories, and spoken mock interviews with a timer and scorecard.
- **Helps with the hard parts:** offers and negotiation, a plan after a layoff, the weekly record unemployment benefits ask for, applications in other languages, and searches while employed, in hourly work, freelance or academia.
- **Shows it all as pages** in your browser: a dashboard, flashcards, a portfolio site and an interview brief, in a look you pick.
- **In Claude, panels** for your Outbox, job board, contacts, new leads, application answers and mock interviews. Codex does the same in the chat.
- **Optional automatic checks:** a morning job scan, an inbox check, follow-up drafts or a weekly review on your own computer. They only read, draft and track.
- **Your other connected apps** (company data like PitchBook, Google Drive, meeting notes) and your **alumni network** can help, read only, if you have them.

## What it won't do

- **Send anything or submit applications on its own.** You send and submit. A safety check in both apps blocks the assistant from sending email, inviting people to events, using the browser on Gmail, Outlook or LinkedIn, or pushing your folder to a public GitHub repository.
- **Make things up.** If a job wants a skill you don't have, it says so.
- **Touch LinkedIn for you.** It drafts; you paste.
- **Phone home.** No server, no account, no telemetry. The AI company running the app (Anthropic or OpenAI) does see what the assistant reads: [where your information goes](https://github.com/ClarvAI/job-search-hq/blob/v1.0.0/docs/privacy.md).

## Good to know

- **The safety check is a backstop, not a guarantee.** It runs only in a folder you've trusted (and in Codex, after you approve its hooks), and it can't see everything, such as inside a script saved in a file or sites other than GitHub. [What it covers and what it doesn't](https://github.com/ClarvAI/job-search-hq/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#what-the-safety-check-covers).
- **The panels are built on Claude Code mods,** a new feature that may change. Their buttons are in English only. Without them, everything works in the chat.
- **Automatic checks** run only while the desktop app is open and the computer is awake.
- **Other apps:** a regular Claude chat with a folder attached, and personal assistant apps, aren't supported. Assistants like Cursor or Gemini CLI get the written rules but not the safety check: [platforms](https://github.com/ClarvAI/job-search-hq/blob/v1.0.0/docs/platforms.md).
- **Accessibility:** we aim for WCAG 2.2 AA and haven't yet tested with real assistive technology: [what was checked](https://github.com/ClarvAI/job-search-hq/blob/v1.0.0/docs/accessibility.md).
- **Your files stay yours.** They're never part of a download and an update never changes them. Say "back up my stuff" any time for a dated zip.

## Updating later

When a new version comes out, download its `job-search-hq.zip` and say **update** in the app. Only the app's files change, your edits to app files are kept as `<file>.local`, and "undo the update" rolls back.

## Checking the download (optional)

The `.sha256` file holds a fingerprint of the zip. To compare, run this in the folder you downloaded to and check that the long code matches the one in the `.sha256` file:

- Mac (Terminal): `shasum -a 256 job-search-hq.zip`
- Windows (PowerShell): `Get-FileHash job-search-hq.zip`
